explicit_validation.explanation: Paper explicitly validates LLM-as-a-judge against human evaluation by comparing preferences on the same 700 queries using correlation metrics (Pearson Correlation, Cohen's Kappa) and shows strong agreement between model and human judgments

prompts.notes: Exact prompts shown in Appendix Tables 13-15; same instruction/rubric structures as human evaluation with minor adaptations for LLM readability; includes chain-of-thought, in-context learning, and HTML tags

inter_annotator_agreement.interpretation: Majority vote used to mitigate biases; if no majority, default to tie

guidelines.notes: Detailed guidelines provided in Appendix A.6 and Figs. 5-7 (annotation interface); includes definition of aspects, rating categories, and step-by-step guidelines

sample_size.notes: 700 queries subsampled (100 from each of 7 domains) for validation; both LLM and human evaluate identical instances with same criteria

quantitative_scores.notes: Minimum correlation reported; LLM evaluators align well with average human scores
Minimum agreement reported; all correlations show strong agreement

correlation_interpretation.threshold_used: Not explicitly stated, but correlations >0.5 and kappa >0.4 considered strong agreement

validation_results.summary_finding: LLM evaluators show strong correlation (Pearson r≥0.52) and agreement (kappa≥0.43) with human judgments across three criteria, validating RAG-QA ARENA as an efficient and accurate framework; GPT-4-0125-PREVIEW selected as best evaluator

criteria_mapping.notes: LLM and human evaluations use identical three criteria with same definitions and priorities (Truthfulness as primary criterion)
